article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant autoflowering hybrid
Genetics: Purple Kush
Breeder: Buddha Seeds
THC Content: Moderate
CBD Content: Not specified by the breeder
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sandalwood, hash, earth, sweet fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 70 days from seed to harvest
Outdoor Harvest Time: 70 days from germination
Indoor Yield: 350–400 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 50–60 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Purple Kush Auto makes its strongest impression before the flower ever reaches a grinder. As maturity approaches, green tissue can give way to deep violet, burgundy, and purple coloration while a pale layer of resin builds across the flowers. Buddha Seeds developed this automatic cultivar around classic Kush qualities rather than contemporary candy-shop excess: dense buds, compact growth, physical relaxation, hash-like depth, and earthy sweetness are central to the experience.

Its fast schedule adds an entirely different advantage. Instead of waiting for seasonal light changes or managing a separate indoor flowering cycle, growers can move from germination to harvest in about ten weeks. The finished weed is consequently aimed at people who want a small, forgiving plant with unmistakably indica character and a visual identity that stands apart from ordinary green autoflowers.
Genetics and Lineage

Buddha Seeds classifies the cultivar as an indica-dominant autoflower with strong Kush heritage, but the company does not currently publish the exact parental formula behind its automatic version. That distinction is important. Numerous websites describe Purple Kush as descending from Hindu Kush and Purple Afghani , and other breeders sell automatic versions built from those parents, but those details should not automatically be assigned to the Buddha Seeds line without breeder confirmation. The most accurate lineage description is therefore a Purple Kush-derived, indica-dominant autoflower developed and stabilized by Buddha Seeds.

Its growth and finished effects strongly reflect that indica direction. Plants remain compact, produce dense resinous flowers, and finish with the physically calming character associated with traditional Kush-type marijuana. Automatic flowering separates it from conventional photoperiod Purple Kush selections because bloom begins according to maturity rather than shortening daylight. This matters when comparing seed catalogs: “Purple Kush Auto” is not one universal genetic formula, and breeder names should remain attached to any claims about yield, potency, or cultivation time.
Effects and Experience

The experience is built around body relaxation rather than rapid cerebral stimulation. Buddha Seeds describes the effect as mildly narcotic and deeply relaxing, language that fits a cultivar intended more for slowing down than increasing activity. Early in a session, mental tension may begin to soften without an especially energetic rush. The body then becomes progressively more noticeable, with limbs feeling heavier and the pace of activity naturally declining.

Compared with some modern high-THC autos, the breeder presents Purple Kush Auto as more moderate in intensity. That can make the strain approachable for consumers who want recognizable indica effects without deliberately chasing extreme potency. Larger servings can still become quite sedating, particularly for people with limited tolerance. This is therefore better suited to evenings, movies , music, or preparing for sleep than demanding daytime tasks. Cannabis can impair reaction time, coordination, perception, and judgment, so even a comfortable body high should never be combined with driving or other safety-sensitive activities.
Medical Benefits

The cultivar’s slow, body-centered character may interest some medical marijuana consumers looking for an evening-oriented product. Buddha Seeds specifically associates the strain with relaxation and describes it as appealing to people seeking relief related to pain, stress, or sleeplessness. Those descriptions reflect traditional and consumer-oriented use rather than proof that Purple Kush Auto treats a medical condition. No clinical trial has established this particular breeder-specific cannabis strain as a standardized therapy.

Moderate potency may be an advantage for patients who find very high-THC flower unnecessarily intense, but individual response remains unpredictable. The breeder does not publish a cannabinoid laboratory panel for the current seed line, so consumers should rely on testing from the actual harvested product whenever available. Anyone using cannabis alongside prescription medications or for persistent pain, sleep problems, anxiety, or other health conditions should discuss marijuana use with a qualified healthcare professional rather than relying on strain reputation alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Where many purple cultivars emphasize grape candy or berry syrup, this plant stays closer to traditional Kush. Buddha Seeds lists soft sandalwood and hash tones in its technical specifications, while the broader description adds earthy, fruity, and sweet nuances. A freshly opened flower may therefore begin with dry earth and woody incense, followed by a darker hash-like quality and restrained fruit sweetness. The aromatic character is warm and grounded rather than aggressively sugary.

No official terpene percentages are currently published for this version, so assigning a dominant myrcene, caryophyllene, limonene, or pinene profile would require borrowing data from unrelated Purple Kush cultivars. The more authoritative approach is to preserve the breeder-supported sensory profile. Sandalwood provides a dry woody impression, hash contributes resinous depth, and the fruit-and-sweet component rounds out the heavier earthy base. Drying and curing quality will determine how clearly those layers survive into finished cannabis.
Growing Information

Cultivation is where Purple Kush Auto becomes especially practical. Buddha Seeds lists a total growth-and-flowering cycle of approximately 70 days, allowing growers to complete a crop without managing a photoperiod transition. Indoor yield is rated at 350–400 g/m², while outdoor production averages roughly 50–60 g per plant. The breeder emphasizes a compact, sturdy structure, making the cultivar useful in small indoor gardens, balconies, terraces, or other situations where vertical space is limited.

Dense resinous flowers develop along a stout indica frame, and purple coloration can become increasingly dramatic as maturity approaches. Buddha Seeds explains that anthocyanin pigments are responsible for red, blue, and purple tones in cannabis and that genetics strongly influence whether those pigments appear. Cooler late-flowering temperatures can make purple coloration more visible as chlorophyll production declines, although color itself does not determine cannabinoid potency.

The plant is described by its breeder as resilient, adaptable, and beginner-friendly. Indoor or outdoor cultivation is possible, and the automatic schedule eliminates the need to switch lighting to 12 hours of darkness. Even so, autoflowers reward careful early growth because their biological schedule keeps moving regardless of stress. Overwatering , root disturbance, excessive feeding, or aggressive pruning during the first few weeks can reduce final size. Gentle training, consistent irrigation, good airflow, and stable environmental conditions are generally better suited to such a short-lived plant.
FAQ
Is Purple Kush Auto indica or sativa?
Buddha Seeds identifies its version as an indica-dominant autoflower. Its compact growth, dense flowers, and deeply relaxing physical effect all reflect that indica influence.
What are the genetics of Purple Kush Auto?

The Buddha Seeds version comes from Purple Kush-derived autoflowering genetics, but the breeder does not publicly disclose the exact parental cross. It should therefore not automatically be labeled Hindu Kush × Purple Afghani × ruderalis unless discussing a different breeder’s version.
How strong is Purple Kush Auto?

Buddha Seeds describes its THC level as moderate rather than extreme but does not currently publish a numerical percentage. Potency should therefore be judged from laboratory testing of the actual harvested cannabis rather than an unverified universal figure.
How long does Purple Kush Auto take to grow?
The breeder lists approximately 70 days for the complete growth and flowering cycle. Because it is an autoflower, flowering begins according to plant age rather than a change in daylight duration.
How much does Purple Kush Auto yield?

Buddha Seeds lists approximately 350–400 g/m² indoors and 50–60 g per plant outdoors. Actual harvest weight depends on light, climate, root development, nutrition, plant health, and overall growing conditions.
Final Thoughts on Purple Kush Auto

Purple Kush Auto is built around simplicity and traditional indica character rather than record-breaking potency. Buddha Seeds combines a compact automatic growth pattern with dense resin production , striking purple coloration, earthy sweetness, sandalwood, and hash-like flavor. Its physical effects follow the same old-school direction, emphasizing calm and relaxation over energetic cerebral stimulation. Most notably, the entire crop can reach maturity in approximately 70 days while still producing up to 350–400 g/m² indoors.

Accuracy is particularly important with this cultivar because several breeders market their own versions of Purple Kush Auto. Buddha Seeds does not disclose an exact parental cross or numerical THC value, and those unknowns are preferable to filling gaps with specifications taken from unrelated seed lines. Within the breeder information that is available, the plant has a clear identity: compact, easy-growing purple weed with moderate potency, strong indica influence, a short automatic schedule, and a distinctly earthy, hash-oriented Kush personality.
